true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition silently replaces the width/height API

Ruby keeps only the last def self.downsize. The new 3-argument form at line 149 replaces the width/height form at line 145, so that method is dead. Existing callers of OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts) now bind max_height to opts. optimize then evaluates opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer and raises NoMethodError, and any resize geometry built from the numeric width is lost. Call sites that still pass width and height (thumbnail/downsize code outside this diff) will break at runtime.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client upload cap ignores per-type site settings

validateUploadedFile used to enforce Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so images and attachments honored separate admin limits. It now always uses 10*1024 KB. Attachments larger than 10MB are rejected even when max_attachment_size_kb is higher, and images cannot exceed 10MB even when max_image_size_kb is higher (or 0, which this codebase treats as "do not enforce"). The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hardcode, so the file_too_large dialog reports 10240 KB regardless of the limit that actually rejected the upload.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
In-place downsize uses the open tempfile path and ignores failure

OptimizedImage.downsize is called with the same path for input and output (tempfile.path, tempfile.path). ImageMagick convert cannot safely read and write the same file: it typically truncates the output before the input is fully read, producing an empty or corrupt image, or it replaces the inode while the open Tempfile fd still refers to the old file. Upload.create_for is then given that same tempfile and tempfile.size, so it can store the truncated/stale bytes rather than the resized image. The path also has no image extension (Rack/URL tempfiles are extensionless), so convert often cannot pick an output format, and the GIF branch never runs because optimize only treats a path matching /\.GIF$/i as animated. "80%" is also not a valid gifsicle --resize-fit size, so animated GIFs fail even when the extension is present. The return value is ignored and the loop does not reject the upload if the file is still larger than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb after five attempts, so a failed or insufficient shrink still proceeds to Upload.create_for.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Multipart uploads are resized with no server-side size cap

URL fetches were changed to a fixed 10.megabytes limit, but the new downsize loop on the multipart path has no upper bound. It runs ImageMagick (and ImageOptim inside convert_with) up to five times on any image larger than max_image_size_kb. The 10MB check exists only in client JS, which a direct POST or API upload can skip. A large or decompression-bomb image therefore reaches convert before Upload.create_for can reject it, tying up the deferred upload worker and memory.

No test covers automatic downsize-on-upload

The new shrink-before-create path has no test. A regression test would need an image over max_image_size_kb (including a GIF and an extensionless uploaded tempfile), assert the stored file is a valid image under the limit with updated filesize/dimensions, and assert that a failed or still-too-large downsize is rejected instead of saved. Without that, the in-place convert failure and the overridden downsize signature will not be caught.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blank host raises in before_validation

before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil guard and there is no presence validation. Creating or updating with a missing host (the controller assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` straight through) raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, so the admin request 500s rather than returning the JSON error the UI expects.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing

update and destroy load the row with `where(id:).first` and immediately call save_host or destroy. A stale or unknown id yields nil, so `host.host = ...` or `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError and the admin API returns 500 instead of 404. The new controller specs only assert the class ancestry, so this path is untested.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Host allowlist match is case-sensitive on the input

record_for_host queries `lower(host) = ?` but binds `uri.host` without downcasing, and before_validation never downcases the saved host. Ruby's URI preserves case, so `lower('Example.com') = 'Example.com'` is false. A mixed-case saved host never matches, and a mixed-case Referer or embed URL never matches a lowercase row, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? and per-host category lookup fail closed and comments/import are rejected.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are raw SQL and not normalized

Existing allowlist entries are inserted with string interpolation (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) and are not run through EmbeddableHost normalization. A host containing a quote aborts the migration (or injects SQL). Values that the old setting accepted, such as `http://example.com`, `example.com/path`, or a trailing `\r`, are stored verbatim. Lookups compare URI#host (`example.com`) to that stored string, so previously working embeds stop matching, and the migration then deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category settings so there is no source left to repair from. The `change` method's raw `execute` calls are also not reversible.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

Existing allowlist entries are inserted with string interpolation (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) and are not run through EmbeddableHost normalization. A host containing a quote aborts the migration (or injects SQL). Values that the old setting accepted, such as `http://example.com`, `example.com/path`, or a trailing `\r`, are stored verbatim. Lookups compare URI#host (`example.com`) to that stored string, so previously working embeds stop matching, and the migration then deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category settings so there is no source left to repair from. true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category is unset

The migration does `execute(...)[0]['id']` on the embed_category name join, and the same pattern again for uncategorized_category_id. Discourse only writes site_settings rows when a setting is overridden, so a typical site has no embed_category row and this raises NoMethodError on nil before any fallback. A case mismatch or a setting that is not exactly a category name fails the same way. The upgrade cannot finish, so the new embeddable_hosts table is never created and embedding stays broken.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Duplicate hosts are allowed and category lookup is ambiguous

There is no uniqueness validation and the migration creates no unique index on host. Two rows for the same host (double-submit, or duplicate lines in the old setting) both save. record_for_host uses an unordered `.first`, so topic import can attach either category nondeterministically, which defeats the per-host category feature.

Hosts with ports can be saved but never match

The format validator explicitly allows `:port`, and before_validation only strips the scheme and path, so `example.com:8080` is stored. record_for_host then uses `uri.host`, which drops the port, and compares that to the stored value. A referer of `http://example.com:8080/...` therefore never matches the row the admin just saved, so that host is never treated as embeddable and never supplies a category.

New host CRUD and migration behavior are untested

Admin::EmbeddableHostsController and Admin::EmbeddingController specs only check that the class subclasses AdminController. Nothing covers create, update, destroy, missing ids, blank host, category assignment, or the data migration. The expandable_first_post? example named "is false if embeddable_host is blank" also no longer sets embed_truncate or stubs an embed, so it passes for unrelated reasons and does not lock the new contract.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe 500s when the user has no TopicUser row

unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then reads tu.notification_level with no nil check. TopicView succeeding only means the user can see the topic; it does not create a topic_users row. Any logged-in user who opens /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe for a topic they have never visited (or whose row was removed) gets NoMethodError instead of being muted. That URL is publicly linked from email and is not restricted to people who already have a TopicUser.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Direct save skips notifications_reason_id so auto-track can undo the change

The new level is written with tu.notification_level= and tu.save! instead of TopicUser.change. change is what sets notifications_changed_at, notifications_reason_id (user_changed), and the MessageBus notification_level_change event. update_last_read in topic_user.rb promotes notification_level back to tracking whenever notifications_reason_id is still null and time-on-topic exceeds the auto-track threshold. Users who were at the default regular level (reason id null) and get muted here will be bumped back to tracking the next time post timings are recorded, so the unsubscribe does not stick. Other open tabs also never hear about the change.

No spec covers the unsubscribe action or the new email link

The only test change is in spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb, which passes unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe" so I18n interpolation of the rewritten unsubscribe_link string does not raise. It never asserts that the per-topic sentence or URL is actually in the body. There is no controller or mailer spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus regular, slug redirect, or that notification emails include topic.unsubscribe_url. The non-idempotent level change and the nil crash can ship unnoticed.

Topic unsubscribe changes state on an unauthenticated GET

TopicsController#unsubscribe is routed only as GET (config/routes.rb) and immediately writes TopicUser.notification_level. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, and the link embedded in notification emails carries no per-recipient token. Any page that can make the browser request that URL while the victim is logged in (an img or link on another site, a link previewer in the same browser) will change that user's notification level using their session cookie. The link is also not bound to the mailbox recipient, so on a shared browser it mutates whichever account happens to be logged in, not the person who was emailed. Because the transition is not idempotent (watching/tracking becomes regular, a second fetch then mutes), a refresh or a second request does not even settle on the same level.

Unsubscribe template path does not match the Ember route

The route is registered as top-level topicUnsubscribe (app-route-map.js.es6), and the controller and view are named topic-unsubscribe, so Ember looks up the template topic-unsubscribe. This file lives at templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which compiles to the template name topic/unsubscribe used only by a nested topic.unsubscribe route. Nothing in the route calls renderTemplate to point at that name. After the server action runs, the Ember app transitions to topicUnsubscribe and renders a missing template: the confirmation text and the topic-notifications-button never appear, so the user gets a blank page and cannot correct the level the GET just wrote.

Watching and tracking users are not actually unsubscribed

If notification_level is above regular (tracking=2 or watching=3), the action sets regular (1); only regular or muted users are set to muted. Regular still emails replies, mentions, and quotes, and watching is exactly the level that emails every new post. The email copy in server.en.yml tells the recipient this link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and the confirmation string in client.en.yml always says they will stop receiving notifications. After one click a watcher is only demoted to regular, so those emails continue, and the confirmation is false. A second request (refresh, or the non-idempotent GET being fetched twice) then takes the else branch and mutes, so the end state depends on how many times the URL was hit.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
should_block? write clobbers the row and double-counts

BlockedEmail.should_block? loads a row, increments match_count in memory, and record.save writes every attribute back. That is last-write-wins with no row lock and no atomic UPDATE match_count = match_count + 1, so a concurrent admin change to action_type (for example switching block to do_nothing) can be overwritten by an in-flight check, and overlapping checks lose increments. The write also runs inside email validation, and UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so one signup attempt runs the validator twice and adds 2 to match_count whenever any BlockedEmail row matches, including action_type do_nothing. A frequently submitted blocked address becomes a hot-row write on every attempt, and the new specs only call should_block? once so they still expect a +1 change.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain allow/deny regex is not anchored

email_in_restriction_setting? compiles Regexp.new("@(#{domains})") with no end anchor after only escaping dots. For a whitelist entry example.com, user@example.com.evil.com matches because @example.com is only required as a substring, so the address is treated as allowed and signup proceeds. The same helper is now the only domain check on User. Other regex metacharacters in the site setting are also unescaped, so a malformed domain list can raise RegexpError and 500 registration instead of failing validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email match is exact and case-sensitive

should_block? uses BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first, and the unique index on blocked_emails.email is case-sensitive. Elsewhere this app canonicalizes addresses with Email.downcase and strip (UsersController#change_email) before comparing, but signup validation neither normalizes the submitted address nor the stored block row. A block for blocked@spam.com therefore does not match Blocked@spam.com, surrounding whitespace, or other case variants, and those addresses pass validation and can register. Uniqueness on BlockedEmail has the same comparison, so both casings can be stored as separate rows and .first still only sees an exact match.

false_positives.candidate:
Any rejected email is shown as an invalid format

On a failed create, any result.errors.email causes the submitted address to be pushed onto rejectedEmails. emailValidation then always fails with I18n.t('user.email.invalid'), the format-failure string, whether the server rejected a blocked address, a disallowed domain, or a duplicate. The new server string user.email.blocked is never shown on the field. The address also stays rejected for the life of the controller, so a transient 'already taken' failure cannot be retried without a full reload.

Moved domain rules and block wiring are untested

The EmailValidator examples stub BlockedEmail.should_block? and only check whether an error was added. They never set email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist, so the domain-restriction logic moved out of User#email_validator can break without a failing test. Nothing exercises User save or UsersController#create with a real BlockedEmail row, so a case-variant bypass or a double match_count increment on valid? plus save would also pass CI.

blocked_emails migration is not reflected in schema.rb

This migration creates blocked_emails, but db/schema.rb is not updated. Discourse loads fresh and test databases from schema.rb (db:schema:load / db:test:prepare) rather than replaying every migration. New environments and CI will not have the table, so BlockedEmail.should_block? and the new specs will raise a missing-relation error until the schema dump is regenerated and committed.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin

The iframe sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `postMessage`'s targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not the full referring URL. A path or query on the referer means the parent origin does not match, the resize message is dropped (or the call throws), and `embed.js` never updates `#discourse-embed-frame` height, so comments are clipped by `scrolling="no"`. The same interpolation is only HTML-escaped, not JavaScript-escaped, so a referer whose host is the configured embeddable host but whose path contains a quote (Rails 3 does not escape `'`) or a JS line terminator breaks out of the string and runs in the forum origin.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Imported HTML is stored and rendered unsanitized

RSS and remote imports create the topic with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`. `Post#cook` then returns `raw` unchanged, skipping the normal cook/sanitize pipeline, and both the topic page and `embed/best.html.erb` (`raw post.cooked`) emit that HTML. `PollFeed` feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML` of the feed item straight into this path, and `import` also interpolates the source URL into an `<a href='...'>` without escaping. A feed item or fetched page can therefore store script or a broken-out URL (`http://host/'><script>...`) that runs in the forum origin for every visitor.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has invalid ERB and will not render

The header conditional is closed with `<%- end if %>`, which compiles to invalid Ruby (`end if` with no condition) and raises a syntax error when the embed layout renders `best`. Any request that finds an existing topic therefore 500s instead of showing highlights, so the embed iframe never works for topics that have already been imported. It needs to be `<% end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes on typical RSS items and blocks embeds

`i.content.scrub` assumes every item has a `content` field and that `String#scrub` exists. Standard RSS 2.0 items only have `description`, so `i.content` is nil and this raises NoMethodError; `scrub` itself is also missing on Ruby 1.9/2.0, which this app still boots. The scheduled job sets `retry: false`, so one bad item aborts the whole import. `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute` synchronously before the HTTP fallback whenever feed polling is enabled, so the same exception also prevents on-demand embed retrieval and leaves the iframe reloading `loading` forever.

true_positives.golden_comment: An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize postMessage uses the full referer as targetOrigin

The iframe sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `postMessage`'s targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not the full referring URL. A path or query on the referer means the parent origin does not match, the resize message is dropped (or the call throws), and `embed.js` never updates `#discourse-embed-frame` height, so comments are clipped by `scrolling="no"`. The same interpolation is only HTML-escaped, not JavaScript-escaped, so a referer whose host is the configured embeddable host but whose path contains a quote (Rails 3 does not escape `'`) or a JS line terminator breaks out of the string and runs in the forum origin.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Disqus import now depends on a live fetch and drops category

The task used to create the topic locally from the export. It now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which `open`s `t[:link]` with no rescue. A single dead link, non-HTTP link, or timeout raises and aborts the rest of the threads (the `ensure` only restores the rate limiter and email blacklist). The `-c`/`category` option and the `category_id` passed to `PostCreator` were removed, and `TopicEmbed.import` has no category argument, so every imported thread lands in the default category instead of the one the operator selected.

Embed success example cannot pass as written

The "topic_id is found" example stubs `TopicView.new` but does not return a topic view (Mocha yields nil). The action then renders `best`, which immediately calls `@topic_view.posts` / `@topic_view.topic`. The shared `after` hook also requires `response.should be_success` and `X-Frame-Options == ALLOWALL`. Even after the `end if` template syntax error is fixed, this example 500s and the new controller spec fails, so it does not lock in the embed response.

Throttle key can stick forever if expire does not run

The per-URL throttle does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and only then `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process dies, the connection drops, or expire fails between those calls, the key is left with no TTL. `retrieved_recently?` then stays true for that embed URL forever (unless the caller is staff and passes `no_throttle`), so the article is never fetched and the embed never leaves the loading state. The set and TTL need to be a single atomic SET with expiry.

Unauthenticated embed fetch is an SSRF and topic-creation primitive

`import_remote` does `open(url).read` with no scheme allowlist, timeout, size limit, or redirect restriction, then publishes the body as a post by `embed_by_username`. `EmbedController#best` will enqueue that fetch for any client that sends `Referer` whose host equals `embeddable_host` (a header the caller sets; it is not a browser-only check) and any `embed_url` on that host. `open-uri` follows redirects, so a redirect on the allowed host makes the app request internal addresses (for example link-local metadata) and can turn the response into a public topic. The same `open` call is also missing `require 'open-uri'`; unless some other file has already loaded it, `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a local path, the retrieve job errors, and the embed stays on the loading page. `TopicRetriever` only calls `Jobs::PollFeed` (which does require `open-uri`) when feed polling is enabled, so the HTTP fallback is the path that breaks.

embed_url is varchar(255) with a unique index

`t.string :embed_url` is a 255-character varchar, and the unique index is on that column. Article URLs with query strings routinely exceed 255 characters. `TopicEmbed.create!` then raises, the import transaction rolls back, and that page can never be embedded. Two distinct URLs that share the same first 255 characters also collide on the unique index and one of them fails to import.

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Header panel is no longer right-aligned without modern flexbox

`.d-header .panel` lost `float: right` and `.d-header .title` lost `float: left`. The replacement is `margin-left: auto` and `order(3)` on the panel, which only pins the controls to the trailing edge when `.contents` is a modern flex container. If `display: flex` (and the 2012 prefixes) are ignored, `.panel` and `.title` are ordinary blocks: auto margins on a width:auto block compute to 0, so the logo and the header controls stack and the controls sit on the left. If the new mixin’s `display: -webkit-box` is what the engine honors, auto margins still do not pack to the end, and the removed floats cannot fall back because that display suppresses float. Login, search, and notification icons are the primary header controls. Keep `float: right` / `float: left` as the non-flex fallback, and do not activate a 2009 box display that disables it.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin writes a 0-based value into 1-based ordinal-group

`@mixin order` assigns the same integer to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` as to `order` / `-webkit-order` / `-ms-flex-order`. The 2009 ordinal-group property is 1-based (initial value 1); `order` is 0-based (initial value 0). The legacy declarations must be `$val + 1`. As written, `@include order(1)` lands in the same group as items that set no order, so it will not sort after them the way `order: 1` does in modern browsers, and `order(0)` is an invalid ordinal-group. Header layout now depends on this mixin (`.panel` uses `order(3)`, `.extra-info-wrapper` uses `order(2)`). Those two values still sort after the default group by accident, but any `order(0)` or `order(1)` — including a plugin rule — will produce a different visual order in old WebKit than in current browsers and scramble the docked header.

false_negatives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
2009 flexbox display values break the layouts that call these mixins

`flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit the 2009 box model (`display: -webkit-box`, `display: -moz-box`, `display: -webkit-inline-box`, `display: -moz-inline-box`) ahead of the 2012/modern values, and they never emit `display: -moz-flex` or `display: -moz-inline-flex`. Engines that only understand the 2009 keywords (Android 4.x stock browser, old iOS) will take that `display` and ignore the later ones. In that model `margin-left: auto` does not absorb free space, modern `align-items`/`order` do not apply, and `float` on the children is suppressed — so there is no float fallback either. That is exactly what the new call sites need: `.d-header .panel` was switched from `float: right` to `margin-left: auto`, and `.badge-wrapper.bullet` previously fell back to the parent `inline-block` when unprefixed `inline-flex` was ignored. Those browsers now drop the header controls (login, search, notifications) off the right edge and lay bullet badges out with the old box model. Firefox 22–27, which only had `-moz-flex`, gets no flex layout at all. Drop the 2009 `display: box` values; they are not a compatible prefix for the properties these call sites use.

Docked topic title can push header controls off-screen

`.extra-info-wrapper` is now a flex item of `.d-header .contents` (`order: 2`, with `.panel` at `order: 3` and `margin-left: auto` so topic info sits between the logo and the controls). Nothing in the new rules sets `min-width: 0`, `overflow: hidden`, or a flex basis on `.extra-info-wrapper` or `.title`, and `.contents` does not set `flex-wrap` (so it stays `nowrap`). Flex items default to `min-width: auto`, which will not shrink below the content’s minimum size. A long docked topic title therefore widens the flex line past the viewport instead of ellipsizing, and `margin-left: auto` cannot pull `.panel` back in — the user menu and notifications are pushed off-screen. Set `min-width: 0` (and overflow/ellipsis on the title child) on `.extra-info-wrapper`.

Small-action row no longer spans the stream or pins its button

`.small-action` is now a flex row, but the action control is still `button { float: right }` (line 309) and `.small-action-desc` changed from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `padding: 0 1.5%` with no `flex: 1` / `min-width: 0`. Float is ignored on flex items, and a float inside a flex item is positioned against that item’s content box, not the full row. The description (or a wrapping `.topic-body`) shrinks to its content, so expand/undo/remove buttons sit beside the text instead of at the right edge of the topic stream. In browsers that do not apply flex, `.topic-avatar` is still `float: left` (line 270) but the 4em padding that cleared that float is gone, so the description overlaps the icon. Vertical spacing was also removed (`margin-top: 5px`, `padding-top: 4px`, and custom-message `margin: 5px 0`), so multi-line custom messages are flush with the row edges. Give the text column `flex: 1` and `min-width: 0`, pin the button with `margin-left: auto` if it is a flex item, and keep a non-flex padding fallback so the text does not cover the avatar.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
website_name bypasses TL0 anonymous website redaction

website, location, and bio are omitted for trust-level 0 users viewed anonymously via untrusted_attributes (include_<attr>? returns false when scope.restrict_user_fields? is true). website_name is derived from that same website value and is not in that list. The new include_website_name method is also never called: ActiveModel Serializers only invokes include_website_name? (every other hook in this file uses the question-mark form), so the attribute is always serialized. Even renaming the method would not close the hole, because it only checks website.present? and does not apply restrict_user_fields?. The profile template now renders the link from model.website_name instead of a client-side name computed from model.website. Previously the omitted website made that label empty and the link stayed hidden; anonymous visitors will now see the TL0 user's website host and, when the domain check matches, the path. Gate website_name with the same untrusted-attribute rule and cover it in the existing anonymous TL0 serializer spec with a website actually set.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-domain label check is case-sensitive, drops port, and mismatches subdomains

Whether to append the path is decided by case-sensitive equality of URI#host and Discourse.current_hostname, plus a case-sensitive ends_with? / dot-label split. Hosts are case-insensitive, so http://Example.com/docs on an example.com instance fails the match and the path this change is meant to show is dropped. URI#host also strips the port, unlike the removed client logic (website.split("/")[2] kept example.com:8080). A non-default port is therefore labeled example.com or example.com/admin while the href is still http://example.com:8080/..., so the link looks like the forum origin. Matching is asymmetric: forums.example.com shows the path for a website on parent example.com, but example.com does not show the path for https://www.example.com/docs or https://blog.example.com/docs, because those hosts are longer and are not a suffix of the instance host. The else branch's ends_with?("." + website_host) also treats any string suffix as the same site, so a website host of com or co.uk matches ordinary forum hostnames and gets its path appended. Compare downcased hosts, keep a non-default port in the label, and only treat equal hosts or a real parent/child relationship in both directions as the same site.

URI parse failure hides the website link entirely

website_name does URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil and returns nil when parsing fails. The profile template only shows the globe link when model.website_name is present, so a parse failure removes the website from the profile even though model.website is still set. Ruby's URI parser rejects non-ASCII IRIs and unescaped characters, including realistic values such as http://example.com/ü or a URL with a space in the path. The old client label used split("/")[2] and still displayed the host for those strings. Falling back to a host-only label (or an IDN-aware parser) is needed so a path the strict parser rejects does not drop the whole website.

members sets offset = params[:offset].to_i and limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no lower bound and no clamp to the last page, then returns that same offset in meta. Fallback locale files are not loaded on the translation path

Server-side fallbacks cannot work unless the fallback YAML is actually loaded, but I18n.translate only calls load_locale for config.locale. The on-demand loader (load_translations patched to load nothing unless given filenames) will not pull in SiteSetting.default_locale or :en. The new ensure_loaded! helper is only invoked from ApplicationController#set_locale (line 159), so background jobs, mailers, rake tasks, and any I18n.with_locale / I18n.t(..., locale:) call that does not go through that before_filter look up fallback locales in an empty store and treat real English (or site-default) strings as missing. That is the main server-side path this change is for: notification emails run outside ApplicationController. It is worse with the LRU cache: getset memoizes the result of translate_no_cache under a key that does not record which locales were loaded. If a missing-translation handler returns a string (instead of raising), that miss is frozen in the cache, and a later ensure_loaded! cannot repair hot keys. Interpolated lookups (args.length > 0) skip the cache but still do not load the fallback chain. A string resolved via the old site locale is stored under the user locale and reused after default_locale changes. Hot keys stay in the 300-entry LRU indefinitely, so users keep seeing the previous fallback language until restart. false_positives.candidate:

Restore a flush-time cap wired to max_segment_spans, and do not evict the root span.

In-place SET to ZSET change will WRONGTYPE on rollout

Segment keys stay span-buf:s:{project:trace}:span_id, but process_spans now ZADDs and the Lua script uses ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN, while flush uses ZSCAN. Existing keys are Redis SETs. During a rolling deploy, old consumers SADD/SUNIONSTORE/SSCAN and new consumers ZADD/ZSCAN on the same keys, and both get WRONGTYPE. Batches fail, segments already buffered cannot be flushed or merged, and keys sit until TTL. Ship a new key prefix or an explicit migration; do not reinterpret live SET keys as ZSETs.

No test for insert-time eviction or score-preserving merges

Existing buffer tests only insert a handful of spans that share one timestamp and then sort flushed output by span_id. Nothing covers a segment larger than 1000, which scores zpopmin keeps, whether the root/segment span survives eviction, ZUNIONSTORE score behavior on redelivery, or flush of a segment that exceeds max_segment_spans. Those are the behaviors this change adds, and the current assertions would still pass if eviction dropped the wrong spans or the cap never ran.

Redirect walk cap lowered and still writes a partial redirect

The parent-redirect walk used to stop at 10000 with a comment that deeper segment trees would not be joined correctly. It now stops at 1000 and, on exhaustion, still HSETs span_id to whatever intermediate set_span_id it landed on and continues the merge. A chain or cycle longer than 1000 hops is silently attached to the wrong segment instead of being left unjoined or failed. If the cap is only a Redis-latency bound, the script should not persist a truncated redirect.

ZUNIONSTORE sums scores and evicts the wrong spans

The merge from sets to sorted sets uses ZUNIONSTORE with the default AGGREGATE SUM (lines 47 and 53). Span payloads are the members and end_timestamp_precise is the score. On Kafka redelivery, or any merge where the same payload is already in both keys, the scores are added. Later zpopmin (line 63) keeps the highest scores, so redelivered spans look newer than they are and genuinely newer spans are dropped once the segment exceeds 1000. Unions should use AGGREGATE MAX (or otherwise preserve the original timestamp) so eviction order stays the end timestamp.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Eligibility cache key uses process-randomized hash()

The cache key is built with Python's builtin hash() of the project-id tuple. hash() is salted by PYTHONHASHSEED, so the same organization and projects produce different keys in different workers. The shared cache therefore does not reuse another worker's result, and invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a key no other process wrote. Allowlist changes cannot be flushed, and the 60-second cache does not actually avoid repeated option lookups across the fleet. Build the key from a stable digest of the sorted project ids. This also adds a remote cache round-trip to every events-stats request, including spans and transactions that can never upsample.

true_positives.golden_comment: The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Upsampling uses the outer dataset and request query, not the query being run

_get_event_stats decides upsampling from the closed-over dataset and request.GET, ignoring scoped_dataset and the query argument it is about to execute. The dashboard-widget splitter calls this with rewritten queries such as "({query}) AND event.type:transaction" and "({query}) AND !event.type:transaction", and sometimes with the discover dataset while the outer dataset is a metrics dataset. A transaction probe therefore still rewrites count() to sum(sample_weight) whenever the original request looked like an error query, so check_if_results_have_data can see empty weights and save_split_decision persists the wrong discover split. The error-only probe does the reverse: it will not upsample unless the original query string already contained event.type:error, so split error widgets keep raw counts.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental git submodule committed

This adds a gitlink named sentry-repo pointing at a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a (the PR base) and does not add a .gitmodules entry. Merging records a broken submodule in the tree that is unrelated to error upsampling. Checkouts and tools that resolve gitlinks will fail or pull an unintended nested repository.

Factory writes sample_rate, query sums sample_weight

_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate (0.1 in the new stats tests). Nothing in this change sets sample_weight or stores the multiplier 1/client_sample_rate. The new aggregate sums sample_weight, and OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest expects one stored event to count as 10. Summing a rate of 0.1 becomes 0 after toInt64, and a missing sample_weight column fails the query, so the test setup cannot produce the asserted result unless an unshown ingest step inverts sample_rate into sample_weight. The helper also runs for every store_event and overwrites an existing sample_rate whenever that context is present.

Integration tests share a 60s cache and bypass the options mock

is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds using only organization id and project ids. These tests reuse the same two projects and only change the mocked options.get return value, but a cache hit never calls options.get. After test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects stores True, the partial-allowlist and empty-allowlist tests still upsample and assert count == 1, so they fail whenever the test cache retains values (Django locmem does). setUp does not clear the cache, and the unit tests never call the cached function, so this path is untested and order-dependent.

Substring check treats negated and mixed queries as error-only

_is_error_focused_query returns true whenever the raw query string contains "event.type:error". That matches "!event.type:error" and "event.type:error OR event.type:transaction", so those discover queries are treated as error-focused. After every project is allowlisted, count() is rewritten to sum(sample_weight). Transactions do not have that column (or have it null), so a normal negated or mixed stats query either fails in Snuba or returns a wrong count instead of the raw count. The docstring says the check errs on the side of caution; a substring test does the opposite.

sum(sample_weight) zeroes legacy events and truncates fractional weights

upsampled_count is toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce. ClickHouse sum skips nulls, so events stored before sample_weight was set contribute nothing: once a project is allowlisted, historical error buckets become 0 instead of the real count. toInt64 also truncates toward zero, so one event with weight 1/0.3 (about 3.33) is reported as 3, and a float sum of 9.999 becomes 9. Counts are silently low. Aggregate round(sum(ifNull(sample_weight, 1))) so missing weights still count as 1.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Replay error context pairs the wrong events and timestamps

fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore get_multi(...).values(). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id and omits missing keys, so values() is not aligned with error_ids: a missing event shifts later payloads onto the wrong ids, and a non-preserving dict order mislabels every error. It also reads data['timestamp'] as a float and gen_request_data compares that to segment event timestamps. Stored events usually keep an ISO datetime (often under datetime) while rrweb segment timestamps are milliseconds, so the comparison either raises TypeError and fails the summarize request, or orders every error at the start of the log.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Flagged table widgets render empty data

When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, tableResultComponent ignores the widget result and renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData whose data, fields, and units are all empty. The real eventView, fields, metadata, and result.data stay on the old StyledSimpleTableChart branch. Enabling the flag therefore blanks every dashboard table widget instead of showing the query results.

true_positives.golden_comment: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Report age/timestamp validation accepts invalid combinations

validate_timestamp treats age as absent when initial_data.get("age") is falsy, so age=0 (a valid Reporting API value meaning the report was just generated) plus a timestamp is accepted. Field validators also never run when the field is omitted, and neither age nor timestamp is required, so a report with neither time field passes. post() then returns 422 for the entire batch on the first invalid item, so one bad report in a browser batch drops metrics for every valid report in that request.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

false_positives.candidate:
60s auth-refresh deadline skips identities for a day

check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60, but it loops a chunk of up to 100 identities and each one can call the IdP via provider.refresh_identity. check_auth already sets last_synced=now before enqueueing this task. If the worker is killed at the deadline, unfinished identities are not refreshed and will not be selected again until the next AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL (about 22–24 hours), so SSO linked/invalid flags stay stale.

AI summary treats a still-loading project as missing

AiContent now does useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id}) and, before the pending check, returns an error alert whenever replayRecord.project_id is set and project is falsy. That hook returns undefined both while the project store is loading and when the project is actually missing, so the Replay Summary tab shows "Project not found" and never starts the summarize request until a later render happens to have the project cached. A genuine load is indistinguishable from a missing project.

Attribute key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch

useTraceItemAttributeKeys used to always build a TagCollection object (empty when the request failed or returned nothing). It now returns attributes: isFetching ? previous : data from useQuery. On error, isFetching is false and data is undefined, and the first fetch has no previous value, so attributes is undefined. Callers that spread or iterate attributes without a null check throw, and isLoading is tied to isFetching so background refetches also flip loading even when previous data is on screen.

Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the searchQuery branch. With an empty search the full sorted attribute list is returned, so those fields stay visible in the default span attributes tree. Searching cannot find them either, because the same filter drops them before the name match. If they are meant to be hidden, the exclusion has to run before the search filter, not only when a query is present.

PR comment helpers are not on the workflow that calls them

GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow call self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and self.get_environment_info, but both methods were added to CommitContextIntegration. The template helper then calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, while _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration. PR comment workflows do not inherit the integration class, so building a suspect-issue comment raises AttributeError and the GitHub/GitLab comment task fails. Separately, MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE interpolates the title into a markdown link with no escaping, so a title containing ] (typical of exception messages) terminates the link and corrupts the rest of the comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code match is case-sensitive and not trimmed

Stored codes are lowercase hex from `randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`, but login accepts a code only after `replaceAll("-", "")` and a strict `indexOf`. The entry placeholder is `XXXXX-XXXXX`, and people commonly type or transcribe backup codes in uppercase or with spaces. Those inputs fail the match and the user is told the code is incorrect even though it is one of the codes they were shown. The same comparison is copied in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` at the `indexOf` on the submitted backup code, so disabling 2FA with a backup code has the same false rejection. Normalize by lowercasing and stripping every non-hex character before comparing.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code consumption is not atomic

After a matching backup code is found, the handler sets that slot to null and writes the whole encrypted list back with a plain `user.update`. Two concurrent authorize calls can both read the same ciphertext, both observe the code as unused, and both return a successful login. If the requests use two different codes, the later write restores the code the earlier request already consumed, so a one-time code stays valid. Disable can race the same way: a login that read the user before disable completes will write `backupCodes` back after disable nulled them. Consume the code with a conditional update (transaction/`SELECT FOR UPDATE`, or update only where the stored ciphertext is still the value that was read) and retry or fail if the row changed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code login can skip the password

The new backup-code branch in credentials authorize never checks the password. Password verification only runs when `credentials.totpCode` is empty (`if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` above this branch). A request that includes any non-empty `totpCode` (it does not have to be a valid authenticator code) plus a valid `backupCode` therefore skips both the password check and the TOTP check and is logged in. The same `totpCode` flag also bypasses the non-CAL identity-provider rejection. Backup codes are long-lived secrets users download as a text file; with this hole, that file alone is enough for account takeover, including for accounts that were later linked to Google/SAML. The branch must verify the password (for any user that has one) itself, and must not treat a dummy `totpCode` as proof of the first factor.

Backup codes can be dismissed forever after 2FA is already on

2FA is enabled on the server before the backup-code step is shown, and the plaintext codes exist only in this modal's state. `onEnable` (which is what the parent uses to refresh the switch and close the flow) runs only from the Close button. `onOpenChange` is passed straight through to `Dialog` and is not blocked on this step, and Cancel is hidden here, so Escape, overlay click, or the dialog close control dismisses the only view of the codes without calling `onEnable`. There is no later screen to reveal or regenerate codes (existing users with a null `backupCodes` column are told to generate them in settings, which this PR does not add). The user can end up with 2FA on, a settings switch still showing off, and no saved backup codes. Keep the dialog from closing until the user confirms they stored the codes, and call the same completion path as Close.

Copy reports success even when clipboard write fails

`navigator.clipboard.writeText` is not awaited and has no `.catch`, but `showToast(..., "success")` runs immediately. If the clipboard API rejects (permissions policy, insecure context, denied prompt), the user still sees "Backup codes copied!" and an unhandled rejection is thrown. Because this screen is the only time the codes are shown, a false success followed by Close leaves them with no codes. Await the write and show the success toast only after it resolves; surface a failure toast otherwise.

Missing-backup-codes message points at a flow that does not exist

`missing_backup_codes` tells the user "Please generate them in your settings." This PR never adds a regenerate action. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration have `backupCodes` null, and the only way to get codes is to disable 2FA with the authenticator and set it up again. Lost-access login and disable will show this string and send them looking for a control that is not there. The copy should describe that actual recovery path (or the UI should grow a real regenerate action before the string ships).

Tests never log in or disable 2FA with a backup code

The new coverage only clicks download, copy, and close on the setup dialog. Download checks the filename but not the file contents, and copy only waits for the success toast, which is shown even when `clipboard.writeText` fails, so a broken copy still passes. Nothing submits a backup code to credentials authorize or to `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable`, which is the path that can skip the password and that burns codes. The other enable test in this file was not updated to dismiss the new backup-code step at all, and its switch assertion is the one the new comment says passes even when the switch is unchecked, so CI will not catch a setup flow that never finishes. Add a login (and disable) that uses a code from the encrypted `backupCodes` column, including a second use of the same code that must fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback crashes when destination calendar is missing

The Meet-to-Cal-Video fallback now does `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` after destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`. If the array is missing or empty, that value is undefined and this throws TypeError before the booking is created. Previously this was optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), so a Meet event with no destination calendar fell back to Daily. Callers in this PR (confirm, Stripe/PayPal webhooks, reminders) explicitly pass `[]` when no calendar is set, so those Meet bookings will 500 instead of being scheduled.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google update/delete fallback never resolves a calendar id

updateEvent and deleteEvent only use destinationCalendar when externalCalendarId is falsy, and then they search for a calendar whose externalId equals that same falsy value. That find can never match a real calendar. The old code used `event.destinationCalendar.externalId` in this branch. Legacy bookings that have no externalCalendarId on the reference now call the Google API with an undefined calendarId, so reschedule and cancel fail (delete no longer falls back to primary either). The same mistake is in deleteEvent around line 315.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug is stored under the inverted billing flag

Unrelated to calendars, the org create payload changed from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. Self-hosted installs with billing disabled used to persist the org slug immediately and will now create organizations with no slug, so org URLs and subdomain setup do not work. Cloud installs with billing enabled used to keep the slug only as metadata.requestedSlug until billing completed, and will now claim the real slug on an unverified, unpaid org. The requestedSlug ternary next to it is equivalent to the old expression; only the slug condition was flipped.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
One missing calendar credential fails every calendar update

In updateAllCalendarEvents, if a reference has a credentialId that is neither on the EventManager user nor returned with an app slug, `credential` stays undefined and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` is still pushed. That rejection fails Promise.all, and the catch now returns every calendar reference as failed without logging (the `console.error(message)` call was removed, and `message` is unused). One co-host credential that cannot be loaded therefore aborts updates for hosts whose calendar calls were valid, and the failure is invisible in logs. The create path correctly skips a missing credential; the update path should do the same.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

false_positives.candidate:
Collective co-host calendars are dropped in common cases

destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and the later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then no-ops. If the booking owner has no destination calendar but other collective hosts do, none of those hosts get a calendar event. Separately, team calendars are collected only from `users.slice(1)` (around line 990). When the event type itself has a destination calendar, the organizer's personal destination calendar is never added, so the owner host is skipped while other hosts are included. The booking row also connects only `destinationCalendar[0]`, so the persisted booking calendar does not represent the co-hosts either.

Google create falls back to primary and can duplicate events

createEvent now chooses the calendar only by `credentialId === credentialId`, and uses "primary" when that find misses. It no longer uses the destination externalId directly. Destination calendars with a null credentialId, and EventManager's no-credentialId branch that calls createEvent once per credential of that integration (EventManager.ts around line 376), therefore write to primary instead of the configured calendar. Each matching Google credential can insert another primary event. The hangout description patch at line 168 uses `selectedCalendar` without the `|| "primary"` fallback, so that follow-up patch is sent with an undefined calendarId whenever the find misses.

Location updates persist empty calendar reference ids

updateLocation now copies `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId` from the EventResult (`result.externalId` / `result.credentialId`). CalendarManager.updateEvent never sets those fields; it only returns appName, type, success, uid, updatedEvent, and warnings. Previously this path stored `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId` and fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar.credentialId`. Location changes therefore insert booking references with a null calendar id and null credential id (and an empty uid, because update results expose `updatedEvent`, not `createdEvent`). Later cancel/reschedule cannot target the provider event those references were meant to track.

Paid confirmation still creates only the owner's calendar event

Stripe payment success builds destinationCalendar from the booking calendar or the booking user's calendar only, then calls eventManager.create(evt). Collective co-host calendars are never loaded. Paid bookings do not create provider events in handleNewBooking; they are created here, so the collective-host fix does not apply and co-hosts still get no calendar event after payment. The same single-calendar construction is in paypal-webhook.ts around line 152 and in confirm.handler.ts around line 175, which is what requires-confirmation uses before scheduling.

Per-host calendar create still targets only the first destination

createAllCalendarEvents loops over every destination calendar and calls createEvent with that destination's credential, but it always passes the original event whose destinationCalendar array still contains every host. Lark (createEvent around line 128), Office 365 (around line 75), and CalDAV (around line 161) all take only index 0. Co-host credentials therefore write to the first host's calendar id: the call 403/404s, or CalDAV's filter matches nothing and createEvent still returns success without creating an object. The stored reference externalId is the co-host calendar, so later updates and deletes look in the wrong place. Google create does look up by credentialId, but its organizer attendee email is still taken from index 0 (CalendarService.ts line 122), so the co-host event is created as if the first host were the organizer.

Recurring collective cancel deletes the wrong events, repeatedly

The new per-reference loop wraps the old recurring-cancel block unchanged. For each calendar reference, that block ignores the reference just fetched and instead walks every calendar credential on the booking owner, and for each remaining occurrence deletes only the first `_calendar` reference (`find`, not `filter`). Co-host events, whose credentials were loaded from the DB on the non-recurring path, are never deleted. The same delete promises are awaited inside the loop and pushed onto apiDeletes, which is awaited again later, so each remaining occurrence is deleted once per calendar reference and then a second time. A two-host recurring series will error or no-op on the other hosts' calendars and hammer the owner's calendar.

Seat merge deletes only the first host calendar event

When newBookingId is set, the code still does `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes that single calendar event. This PR now stores one calendar reference per collective host, but this merge path was not updated to iterate them. Rescheduling into an existing seated booking removes only the first host's old provider event and leaves the other hosts' events on their calendars.

Video booking references lose credentialId

referencesToCreate now sets `credentialId` only for calendar results and forces `undefined` for every other result. The previous code stored `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results. Video meeting references are therefore saved without the credential that created them. Cancellation only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set and matches a credential, so newly created video meetings will be left running on the provider after the Cal.com booking is cancelled.

Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar to DestinationCalendar[] | null, and that object is spread into BOOKING_* webhook payloads. Existing subscribers that read destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will throw or ignore the field. The PR is marked non-breaking, but the e2e update for BOOKING_REJECTED (null -> []) shows the payload changed. It is also inconsistent across events: handleNewBooking still sends null when unset, while confirm/cancel send []. Consumers cannot rely on either an object or an array.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string refresh_token

After a successful parse, if `refresh_token` is absent the helper writes the placeholder string `"refresh_token"` onto the parsed object and returns it. Callers persist that object. Office 365 merges `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credential (`refresh_token` is optional on its schema, and Microsoft often omits a new refresh token), so a real refresh token is overwritten with `"refresh_token"` and the next refresh fails permanently. Zoom assigns `key.refresh_token = newTokens.refresh_token` the same way once the sync schema does not require a refresh token. The placeholder was meant to satisfy schemas, but it is stored as a live secret.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync token schema requires a literal ZodString property

When credential sharing and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, refresh parsing uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` are the strings `"ZodString"` and `"ZodOptional"`, not a catchall for arbitrary fields. Zod object schemas also strip unknown keys. A normal body such as `{ access_token, expires_in }` therefore fails `safeParse`, and `parseRefreshTokenResponse` always throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Google, Office 365, Zoom, and Salesforce refresh all go through this helper, so enabling the feature breaks token refresh for those apps instead of accepting an access token plus expiry.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google token refresh persists the Zod result, not the credential

After a Google refresh, the code assigns `key` to the return value of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` and writes that object to `credential.key`. That helper returns the whole `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: ... }`), not the parsed token. Previously this path saved `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which is the token itself. The next `GoogleCalendarService` construction calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` and throws, so every successful Google token refresh (credential sync off or on) corrupts the stored credential and breaks Google Calendar until the user reconnects. On the sync path this is worse: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a Fetch `Response`, which has no `.data`, so `token.access_token` throws before a valid token can be applied.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync refresh returns an unparsed Fetch Response to callers that expect tokens

When sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` POSTs to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and returns the raw Fetch `Response` without checking `response.ok` or reading JSON. Callers do not share one return type. Google reads `res.data.access_token` (Gaxios shape). HubSpot treats the result as a HubSpot token (`accessToken`, `expiresIn`) and writes it back as `credential.key`. Zoho CRM and Zoho Bigin read `tokenInfo.data` on an axios response. Lark passes the body to `handleLarkError`, which expects a Lark envelope (`code`, `data.refresh_token`, `data.expires_in`). The comment says the endpoint returns only an access token and expiry, but none of these callers adapt that shape, so a successful sync response still fails or stores a Response/wrong object. The non-sync branch returns whatever `refreshFunction` returns, so the two branches are not interchangeable.
