true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential webhook leaves invalid rows invalid and can duplicate credentials

The update path writes only `key`. Credentials previously marked `invalid: true` by a failed refresh stay invalid, so a successful sync from the parent app does not restore the integration. The lookup is also a non-transactional `findFirst` by `userId` + `appId` followed by create (lines 62-90). There is no unique constraint handling, so concurrent webhook deliveries (retries) can insert a second credential for the same user and app. Calendar code uses `findFirst`, so later refreshes update an arbitrary row and the other keeps stale tokens. `zod` parse, `symmetricDecrypt`, and `JSON.parse` are also uncaught, so a bad body or ciphertext becomes an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Outbound token sync request is unauthenticated

The refresh call that is supposed to retrieve a user's third-party access token sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in a form body. It does not send `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, a signature, or any other credential, even though the new inbound webhook authenticates with that secret. Anyone who can reach `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` can request access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user ids. The sample client is what self-hosters are told to point at their token endpoint, and nothing in this request tells that endpoint the caller is Cal.com.

Teams refresh replaces the whole credential with the sync body

After `refreshOAuthTokens`, the MS Teams adapter JSON-parses the response and saves that object as the entire `credential.key`. The sync contract is only an access token and expiry, so this drops `refresh_token`, `email`, and `scope` from the stored credential. Expiry is computed as `Date.now() + (expires_in || 0) * 1000`; if the sync payload uses a different expiry field, `expiry_date` becomes now and every subsequent call treats the token as expired and refreshes again, rewriting the key each time. With sync disabled the Microsoft token response is a full token object, so this only breaks the new sync path, but that path is what this PR adds.

Webex sync refresh still requires a full Webex token body

Webex was switched to `refreshOAuthTokens` but still validates the body with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires `token_type: "Bearer"`, an exact scope literal, `refresh_token`, and `refresh_token_expires_in`. It does not use `parseRefreshTokenResponse`. A sync endpoint that returns only an access token and expiry, as `refreshOAuthTokens` documents, fails this schema and the refresh rejects with "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", so Webex credential sync cannot succeed.

Zoom sync uses app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom

The Zoom refresh calls `refreshOAuthTokens` with app slug `"zoomvideo"`. The installed app id written by the Zoom OAuth callback is `"zoom"` (`appId: "zoom"`), and every other integration in this PR passes its real app slug (`google-calendar`, `msteams`, `office365-calendar`, `hubspot`). The parent store will not find a Zoom credential for `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token sync returns the wrong app or nothing while other apps sync.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest filter misses blacklist, case, and in-request duplicates

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased, but each submitted guest is tested with includes(guest) and compared to existing attendees with guest === attendee.email, with no toLowerCase or trim. Zod's email check allows mixed case, so Spam@blocked.com bypasses a blacklist entry of spam@blocked.com, and A@x.com is inserted even when a@x.com is already an attendee. The variable is named uniqueGuests but the filter never dedupes the input, and the schema does not either, so one request can create two Attendee rows for the same address. There is also no unique (bookingId, email) guard around the check-then-insert, so two concurrent calls can both pass the read and insert the same guest twice.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check is AND, so it never matches

Permission is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), but those membership roles are alternatives (the flag is even named isTeamAdminOrOwner, and the bookings UI uses isUserTeamAdminOrOwner). If the roles are mutually exclusive the expression is always false, because a failed admin check short-circuits and a successful admin check then fails the owner check. A team admin or owner who is not the booking host and whose login email is not already an attendee is always rejected with FORBIDDEN, so they cannot add guests to team bookings from the bookings page.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Emails are selected from the raw guest list, not guests actually added

sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array, not uniqueGuests. In sendAddGuestsEmails, every current attendee whose email is in that array receives AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new booking confirmation plus ICS REQUEST) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Submitting an address that was already on the booking therefore sends that person a fresh 'you are scheduled' invite, which calendar clients treat as a new or duplicate event. Addresses that were filtered out as duplicates still match and take the wrong template; only the addresses that were actually inserted should get the scheduled email.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add-guest emails ignore disableStandardEmails

Every other sender in this file checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail before mailing. sendAddGuestsEmails does not take eventTypeMetadata and always emails the organizer, every attendee, and each new guest. The handler loads eventType but never forwards metadata.disableStandardEmails. false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's

updateCalendarAttendees is invoked through an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The booking query already loads booking.user.credentials and the host destination calendar, but those credentials are never used. Anyone allowed by the attendee check (and any team manager, once the role check is fixed) will try to patch the host's calendar event with their own OAuth tokens. That call fails or updates the wrong account, so the new guests never land on the host calendar. The attendee rows are already committed by then, and a retry treats those emails as duplicates and throws emails_must_be_unique_valid, so the calendar update cannot be completed.

Cancelled, pending, past, and no-guest event types are accepted

After the booking is loaded, nothing checks BookingStatus, endTime, or eventType.disableGuests. A direct call can add attendees to a cancelled, rejected, or still-pending booking and sendAddGuestsEmails will mail ICS REQUEST invites marked CONFIRMED, including the video URL and meeting password when a video reference exists. The same path ignores disableGuests, so an event type that turned guests off still accepts invites. Any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee is authorized, not only the host, so a booker can do this even when the host disabled guests. The bookings UI also offers the action for past confirmed rows, because Add guests lives on bookedActions and that menu is rendered for past confirmed bookings in BookingListItem.

Collective/round-robin hosts are never notified or updated

The CalendarEvent built for this flow never sets team (or the other hosts' destination calendars). sendAddGuestsEmails only loops calendarEvent.team.members, so that loop is dead and co-hosts do not get OrganizerAddGuestsEmail. destinationCalendar is only the booking calendar or the single booking.user calendar. On collective or round-robin events, other hosts keep a stale attendee list on their calendars and receive no email that guests were added.

Email failures are swallowed and reported as success

sendAddGuestsEmails is wrapped in try/catch that only console.log's a static string and drops err. The handler then returns { message: 'Guests added' }, and the dialog shows the success toast and closes. If the mailer throws, guests are stored and the calendar may already have been updated, but nobody is notified and the user is told the operation succeeded. The log line does not include the error, so the failure is also invisible in production logs.

Guest list has no maximum, so one call can mass-mail

guests is z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max() and no uniqueness constraint, and addGuests is a plain authedProcedure rather than the bookings procedure used by editLocation. A host or attendee can submit thousands of addresses in one mutation. Each new address becomes an Attendee row and receives AttendeeScheduledEmail with the meeting link and, when present, the video meeting password. That is an authenticated email-spam and meeting-link disclosure path with no cap.

prisma.booking.update createMany inserts attendees immediately, with no transaction around the later calendar update and sendAddGuestsEmails. If updateCalendarAttendees throws, the tRPC mutation fails but the rows stay. The client shows an error, yet a retry filters those addresses out as already attending and, when no other new addresses remain, returns BAD_REQUEST emails_must_be_unique_valid. The guests exist in the database, the host calendar is unchanged, and no notification is sent, with no way to finish the operation for those addresses.

Every added guest is inserted with name: ''. Attendee emails address them as ' <email>' (AttendeeAddGuestsEmail / AttendeeScheduledEmail use `${name} <${email}>`), and the ICS ATTENDEE CN is blank. Some clients drop or mis-file invites with an empty CN, and the organizer subject uses attendees[0].name, which is an empty string when that row is first. The email local-part or the address itself should be stored as the name, which is what booking-time guests already do.

The new mutation changes booking attendees, calendar events, and a multi-recipient email fan-out, and the PR adds no handler or email tests. Nothing covers the admin-versus-owner permission expression, blacklist and case-folding, rejection of seated or disableGuests event types, cancelled or past bookings, or which template is sent to new versus existing attendees. Those branches are where the implementation is wrong, and they will not be caught by typecheck.

seatsPerTimeSlot and seatsShowAttendees are copied onto the calendar event and then ignored. The handler still createMany's Attendee rows with no BookingSeat / seat-reference rows and no capacity check. On a seated event that overbooks the slot, leaves people who do not show up in seat cancellation or no-show flows, and skips per-seat payment. sendAddGuestsEmails then sends AttendeeScheduledEmail with the full attendee list. Unlike sendScheduledSeatsEmails, it never passes showAttendees, so an event type with seatsShowAttendees false leaks every other attendee's name and email to the newly added addresses.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Overlapping crons lose retry increments and can double-send

retryCount is written as reminder.retryCount + 1 from the value read at the start of the loop, not as an atomic increment, and the row is not claimed before twilio.scheduleSMS. This handler awaits Twilio and several DB calls per reminder, so a run can outlast the cron interval and a second invocation loads the same unscheduled rows. Both workers schedule an SMS and both write the same retryCount, so the counter may never exceed 1, the new delete never fires, and the attendee gets duplicate messages. Use an atomic increment and a conditional update (id and scheduled false) to claim the reminder before calling Twilio.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount cleanup deletes unrelated and already-scheduled reminders

The cron deleteMany ORs past-due SMS reminders with retryCount > 1, and that second branch has no method, scheduled, or scheduledDate filter. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP, so the next run of this SMS job deletes every row with retryCount > 1, including non-SMS reminders and SMS reminders Twilio already accepted (scheduled true, referenceId set). Losing referenceId means a later booking cancellation cannot cancel the provider message, and reminders this job does not own can disappear. Restrict the predicate to unscheduled SMS rows (method SMS, scheduled false, retryCount > 1).

false_positives.candidate:
Any two errors permanently drop the SMS reminder

retryCount is incremented in the catch that wraps the whole reminder, not only a rejected Twilio schedule. Profile lookup, booker URL, template rendering, or a DB error after Twilio already returned a SID all count as failures. After two such errors the next cron deletes the row because retryCount > 1. A short outage therefore discards every in-window SMS reminder instead of retrying until the event. If scheduleSMS succeeded and the following update threw, the catch still increments, scheduled stays false, and the next run can schedule a duplicate while the later delete orphans the Twilio messages. Count only definitive send failures, and do not increment once a provider SID exists. If the catch's own update throws, that exception leaves the loop, the handler never responds, and the rest of the batch is skipped.

Missing recipient or empty body retries until the event

retryCount is only updated inside the branch that calls Twilio. If sendTo is missing or the message is empty, the reminder stays scheduled false with retryCount 0 and is selected again on every cron run until scheduledDate is past. That is a permanent failure (no destination never reaches Twilio) and is exactly the infinite reschedule this change is meant to stop, while also keeping the job busy reprocessing the same rows. Treat that path as a failed attempt or delete the reminder.

No tests for retry limit or delete scope

The new delete predicate and retryCount updates have no tests. Nothing checks that EMAIL/WHATSAPP rows and already-scheduled SMS rows (with a provider referenceId) survive cleanup, that an SMS reminder is removed only after two scheduling failures, or that a missing sendTo does not spin until scheduledDate. Those are the paths that drop reminders or fail to stop the infinite cron loop.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
ANY() on JS arrays will fail when team/org SQL runs

Org and team authorization bind id lists as `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` (line 164), `"userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})` (line 168), and `"userId" = ANY(${userIdsFromTeam})` (line 201). Prisma's raw-query engine does not send a JavaScript number array as a PostgreSQL array parameter; it is passed as text such as `[1,2,3]`. PostgreSQL then rejects the statement (`malformed array literal` or `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`) instead of returning bookings. Team and org insights therefore error at runtime. Use scalar binding, for example `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` or `= ANY(ARRAY[${Prisma.join(ids)}]::int[])`, and keep the existing empty-list guard because `Prisma.join([])` throws. The new `$queryRaw` test only executes the user-scope predicate (`"userId" = $1 AND "teamId" IS NULL`), which never uses `ANY`, so this failure is not covered.

Team scope without teamId now typechecks and returns no rows

The constructor previously required `InsightsBookingServiceOptions`, the zod discriminated union that makes `teamId` mandatory when `scope` is `"team"`. It now accepts `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, where `teamId` is optional for every scope. A team-scoped call that omits `teamId` still fails `safeParse`, is stored as `this.options = null`, and `buildAuthorizationConditions` returns `1=0` with no error. Callers get an empty insights result that looks like "no bookings" instead of a compile-time or thrown validation error. Keep the discriminated union on the constructor, or throw when `safeParse` fails, so a missing `teamId` cannot be confused with an authorized empty set.

toEqual(Prisma.sql) does not match composed fragments

Team-scope (line 295), org-scope (line 332), and combined-filter (line 429) expectations are a single flat `Prisma.sql` template. The service builds those predicates with `reduce` into `Prisma.sql`(${acc}) OR/AND (${condition})`, which stores nested `Prisma.Sql` objects in `.values` and only flattens them when the query is executed. Vitest `toEqual` compares `.strings` and `.values` and does not render nested fragments, so these three assertions fail even when the SQL that would be sent is equivalent. User-scope and single-filter tests pass only because those paths return one flat template. Assert a flattened rendering, or build the expected value with the same nesting, otherwise CI cannot validate the composed authorization SQL.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

Every cache fill rewrites all SelectedCalendar rows

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook helper writes the wrong env file and is macOS-only

true_positives.golden_comment: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

Cache timestamp render is not null-safe and ignores locale

cacheUpdatedAt is Date | null | undefined, and assigning isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt to hasCache does not narrow it. new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) is therefore a strict-null type error, and if a null/invalid value is formatted, Intl.DateTimeFormat.format throws RangeError and crashes the whole connected-calendars list. Cache status ignores expiry

Expired rows therefore show a last-updated time and a delete action for data that availability will not use. After the migration backfill, that timestamp is also the deploy time rather than the last real refresh.

deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (or apps.integrations). SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper owns that query with refetchOnWindowFocus: false and passes props.onChanged, which is often undefined and is not a refetch of this query. After a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old "Last updated" time and "Delete cached data" until a full reload, so the action looks like it failed.

Empty actions slot still reserves width

DisconnectIntegration used to be omitted entirely for delegation credentials and when connection changes are disabled. It is now always wrapped in a flex w-32 div, while CredentialActionsDropdown returns null when the user cannot disconnect and there is no cache. Those rows keep an empty 8rem actions column, shifting the calendar card and error alert layout.

dev:cron now depends on undeclared npx tsx

dev:cron changed from ts-node, which is a devDependency of @calcom/web, to npx tsx. tsx is not declared in this package, and the app is on Yarn 3.4.1, where npx is not the project runner. yarn dev:cron will fail offline, in CI images without npm/npx, or by downloading an arbitrary tsx version outside the lockfile. Add tsx as a devDependency and invoke it via yarn, or keep ts-node.

updatedAt backfill marks every existing cache as just written

ADD COLUMN updatedAt TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW() sets every existing CalendarCache row to the migration transaction time. The new UI treats that value as "Last updated", so on deploy every Google calendar with a cache row looks freshly synced even if the row is old or already past expiresAt. now() is STABLE, not a constant, so Postgres cannot use the PG11 fast-default path and will rewrite CalendarCache under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. The header comment also says the column was added without a default, which is the opposite of this SQL. Backfill from a real write time (or leave the column nullable until the next upsert) and avoid a single volatile default on a large table.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete does not persist cancellation or allow retry

When immediateDelete is true, deleteScheduledEmailReminder POSTs a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder. handleNewBooking.ts line 968 uses this for every reschedule, and workflows.tsx uses it when a workflow or step is deleted (then cascade-deletes the rows). If SendGrid rejects the cancel — including the 100 pending-cancellation cap this PR exists to avoid — the error is only logged, cancelled stays unset, and the cron will never retry, so the email still sends. On success the cancel status still sits in scheduled_sends until the original send time, so reschedules keep filling that same 100 cap. Callers also fire this inside forEach without await, so the HTTP call can still be in flight when the mutation returns and, on workflow delete, when the referenceId row is cascade-deleted. Reschedule should use the deferred cancelled flag (and only cancel immediately when the send is inside the cron gap); immediate cancel must be awaited and must leave a retryable record if SendGrid fails.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for the cancellation fix that already failed once

This PR replaces the SendGrid cancel path after #6991 did not stop reminders for cancelled and rescheduled bookings, but it adds no tests. Nothing covers: cancelled=true is set instead of calling SendGrid on booking cancel, the cron cancels only due reminders and does not delete them first, a SendGrid error does not abort the rest of the batch, reschedule does not lose the reminder when the immediate cancel fails, and paid cancels do not skip cleanup. Those are the paths that still send email if wrong.

One SendGrid cancel error skips the rest of the batch

All cancellations share one try/catch around the for-loop. client.request is awaited per reminder, but the prisma deletes are only executed after the entire loop via Promise.all. The first non-2xx response — an unknown batch id, an already-cancelled batch, a null referenceId, or the 100-cancellation limit — jumps to the catch, so later reminders are not cancelled and none of the already-successful cancels are deleted from WorkflowReminder. Those rows stay cancelled=true and are processed first on the next run, which can block every subsequent reminder until their scheduledDate passes and the opening deleteMany drops them without a SendGrid cancel. Handle each reminder independently, delete the row only after that reminder's cancel succeeds, and continue after a failure.

Overdue cancelled reminders are deleted before SendGrid is cancelled

The cron deletes every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is already <= now before it looks up cancelled reminders. The cancel query only then loads rows with cancelled=true and scheduledDate <= now+1 hour, so any cancelled reminder whose send time has passed is already gone and never gets POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends status=cancel. Booking cancellation only sets cancelled=true and does not call SendGrid (handleCancelBooking.ts around the deleteScheduledEmailReminder call). Combined with a cron that the PR says runs every 15 minutes, a booking cancelled after the last tick before the reminder (or any missed run that returns after scheduledDate) still delivers the email, and the tracking row is removed so a later run cannot retry. Cancel SendGrid first, including slightly overdue cancelled rows, and do not delete those rows until the cancel succeeds.

Paid cancellations return before workflow reminders are cancelled

If bookingToDelete.paid is true, the handler refunds and returns "Booking successfully cancelled." at line 464. The reminder cleanup that sets cancelled or deletes WorkflowReminder rows is only reached later (lines 484-493). Paid cancellations therefore never mark or remove email/SMS reminders. Already-submitted SendGrid batches still send, and unscheduled reminders are picked up by scheduleEmailReminders. Move reminder cancellation above this return, on the same path as the unpaid cancel.

Unscheduled reminder query ignores cancellation and booking status

The query that actually submits emails to SendGrid filters only method=EMAIL, scheduled=false, and scheduledDate within 72 hours. It does not exclude cancelled=true and does not check booking.status. Any leftover unscheduled reminder for a cancelled or rescheduled booking is therefore scheduled and sent. That leftover is guaranteed for paid cancellations, which return before reminder cleanup (handleCancelBooking.ts line 464), and also happens if the un-awaited reminder delete loses the race with this cron. Re-check cancelled and booking status immediately before sgMail.send, and skip or delete those rows.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule calendar/video cleanup is not awaited

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) starts async work and immediately returns. getCalendar is now async (it awaits a dynamic import) and deleteMeeting is async, but nothing awaits the forEach callbacks, and the values they return (including calendar.deleteEvent) are discarded. The try/catch around forEach cannot see rejections from those callbacks. Reschedule then sends the reschedule email and returns true while deletions may not have started. On a serverless runtime the process can freeze after the handler returns, so the old calendar event and video meeting are left in place after the booking is already marked CANCELLED, and failures surface only as unhandled rejections.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

false_positives.candidate:
Cancelling remaining recurring events drops calendar deletes

When all remaining recurring instances are cancelled and a credentialId is present, calendar deletion is done with credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(await calendar.deleteEvent(...)) }). The async callbacks are never joined. Later, await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) runs while apiDeletes is still empty, because pushes happen only after getCalendar and deleteEvent resolve inside the detached callbacks. Those pushes also store settled results, not in-flight promises, so they cannot be tracked. Recurring bookings are marked CANCELLED and cancellation email is sent, but the external calendar events for those instances are not reliably deleted; import or API errors become unhandled rejections. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly rewritten to for...of and pushes the delete promise before awaiting; this branch needs the same treatment.

WipeMyCal reschedule cleanup is not awaited

Same control-flow bug as the Vital reschedule handler: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) does not wait for getCalendar, calendar.deleteEvent, or deleteMeeting. Because getCalendar now awaits a dynamic app import before deleteEvent is even called, the deletion often has not started when this function sends the reschedule email and returns true. The surrounding try/catch does not catch async failures. Result: the booking is cancelled in the database while the external calendar event and video meeting can remain, blocking the slot and leaving a stale invite.

requestReschedule returns before integrations are deleted

requestReschedule marks the booking CANCELLED, then uses bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) to await getCalendar and call deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. forEach does not await those promises, and the mutation continues straight into sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks, then resolves. Callers therefore observe success before calendar and video teardown has run. With getCalendar and deleteMeeting now async, the external API calls are no longer even initiated synchronously, so a short-lived server handler can exit first and leave the original event on the calendar and the video meeting alive.

true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Working-hours recheck rejects any split schedule

The new working-hours gate uses Array.find and treats a window as a hit when the slot is outside that window. A host with two windows on the same weekday (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00) therefore fails the check for every slot, because the slot is always outside at least one window, and checkIfIsAvailable returns false. end is assigned the same minutes as start, so the event length is never compared to workingHour.endTime either. This runs for every isFixed user, which includes ordinary personal events, so split-shift availability disappears from the booking page. The inverse is also wrong: if no window lists that weekday, find returns undefined and the slot is not rejected, so a fixed host with no hours that day is still treated as free.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Override containment check is wrong for blocks and multiple ranges

The all-day block branch compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and never succeeds, so a zero-length override (start equal to end) is not treated as blocking the day. A slot that overlaps that instant falls through and is marked available. Separately, dateOverrides.find returns true as soon as any same-day range does not cover the slot, so a second range that does cover it is ignored and the slot is rejected. A slot is also treated as inside a range on any overlap: slot start is not required to be at or after the override start, and slot end is not required to be at or before the override end, so a meeting that only partly fits the override is still offered.

false_positives.candidate:
Date override match skips busy-time checks

When checkIfIsAvailable finds a same-day date override that overlaps the slot, it sets dateOverrideExist and returns true immediately. That return happens before the busy.every() calendar/booking conflict check. The function is used for every fixed host (all users on personal and collective events, and fixed hosts on round-robin) and for loose round-robin hosts. On any day a host has a covering date override, existing bookings and calendar busy times are ignored, so the slot stays bookable and the host can be double-booked.

New tests miss fixed-host overrides and real timezone shifts

The only new assertion re-queries the same personal-event date override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as Asia/Kolkata. That does not cover the PR's main fix (round-robin slot must be hidden when a fixed host's date override makes them unavailable, including when the round-robin host is free). A +30 minute shift also never crosses midnight or a DST boundary, so the hour-wrap and DST bugs in getSlots, and the busy-time skip in checkIfIsAvailable, are not exercised.

Override day match formats local time against UTC

The same-day test compares dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format('YYYY MM DD') with slotStartTime.format('YYYY MM DD'). slotStartTime was created with .utc(), so its format is UTC, but the override side is a local-mode dayjs and formats in the process timezone. On any host whose local timezone is not UTC, the calendar day can differ around midnight, the override is not recognized, and the fixed-host date-override filter either does not apply or applies on the wrong day.

Override minutes are shifted again by today's DST delta

The new override math already converts wall-clock times using utcOffset at override.start for both the organizer zone and the invitee zone, so the resulting minutes are invitee-local on that date. Those minutes are then passed through buildSlots, whose getTime adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff (today's offset minus the target day's offset). That correction exists for weekly hours, which were shifted with today's offset, not for these overrides. When either timezone is in a different DST period today than on the booked day, every override slot moves by that extra delta, typically 60 minutes, so the bookable times do not match the saved override.

Timezone-adjusted overrides lose the day and can invert

Override start/end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced with .hour() and .minute(), which wrap to 0–23 and drop any day the shift crossed. A UTC 22:00–23:30 override viewed in Asia/Kolkata becomes 03:30–05:00 on the invitee's current day instead of the next day. A short early override viewed behind UTC can wrap the end to 00:00 while the start stays late, so startTime >= endTime. buildSlots then skips that range (start >= end), but the code has already removed that user's normal working hours for the day, so the override day shows the wrong slots or none. This is the common case the timezone fix is meant to handle.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sender comparison crashes when metadata has no sender.login

The new check reads integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no guard. build_integration only copies sender into metadata when pipeline state already contains it, and this pipeline never binds sender. Integrations created via the API path, or any row written before sender was stored, therefore have no sender dict. On the re-link path (Integration exists, no OrganizationIntegration, status ACTIVE) a missing or non-dict sender raises KeyError or TypeError. That exception is not caught, so the request 500s instead of the installation error page, and a legitimate reinstall of an integration without sender metadata cannot complete. Look up sender.login safely and fail closed with the authenticity error when it is absent.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

false_positives.candidate:
Installation-not-found test now fails the state check and never hits the 404

test_installation_not_found still replaces /app/installations/{id} with a 404, but the follow-up setup request sends state=ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05. assert_setup_flow in the same file shows a valid pipeline signature is 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3. OAuthLoginView rejects any other state before GitHubInstallation or build_integration runs, so the new assertion that the body contains "Invalid installation request." passes because of the state mismatch, not because a missing GitHub installation is handled. The old "The GitHub installation could not be found." assertion was removed, and nothing else drives get_installation_info's 404 path. A break there would not fail CI. Call back with the pipeline's real signature after a successful token exchange and assert the installation-not-found error again.

Installer identity check is skipped when Integration does not exist yet

GitHubInstallation.dispatch treats Integration.DoesNotExist as success and returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. That is the normal first-install path: the installation webhook often has not created the Integration row before the browser returns with installation_id, and build_integration then creates the Integration and OrganizationIntegration from the caller-supplied installation_id alone. The new comparison of the OAuth login to metadata sender.login only runs after an Integration row already exists and has no OrganizationIntegration. GitHub installation ids are enumerable and webhook delivery is not ordered ahead of the redirect, so an attacker can attach a victim's GitHub App installation to their own Sentry org (or finish the link before the real installer) without ever matching the installer. The control the PR adds fails open on the path it must cover. Finish should be refused until the installer identity is known and matches the OAuth user.

Token exchange omits the redirect_uri sent at authorize time

OAuthLoginView adds redirect_uri to the GitHub authorize URL, but the access-token POST only sends code, client_id, and client_secret. GitHub requires the same redirect_uri on the token request when one was supplied during authorization; otherwise the token endpoint returns redirect_uri_mismatch and no access_token. That response is collapsed into the generic authenticity error, so every install fails whenever the authorize redirect_uri is not treated as the app's default callback. Tests stub the token endpoint and never observe this. Send the same redirect_uri on the exchange. The safe_urlopen call and the following get_user_info call are also outside the try that only wraps the body parse, so a connection error or ApiError from GitHub becomes an unhandled 500 instead of that error page.

User-mismatch test mutates the webhook body but keeps the old HMAC

test_github_user_mismatch changes installation id and sender.login to "attacker" and then posts X-Hub-Signature sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486, which cannot be the HMAC of the mutated body. If the webhook view verifies the signature, the post is 401, the assert status_code == 204 fails, and the Integration sender row the test needs is never created. If verification is off in tests, the signature is meaningless. The later assertion only looks for "Invalid installation request.", which is also returned for a bad OAuth state, a bad code, or a missing login. The setup URL reuses state 9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3 while init_path_2 starts a new pipeline for another organization, so a state failure produces the same page. The test does not show that an OAuth login differing from metadata sender.login is what failed. Recompute the signature for the mutated payload and assert something only the sender comparison path can produce.

installation_id is written into pipeline state before state is validated

OAuthLoginView bind_state's request.GET installation_id before it checks that state equals pipeline.signature, including on requests that have no state at all. PipelineAdvancerView is csrf_protect=False and auth_required=False, and until OAuth finishes the current step is still OAuthLoginView. A cross-site top-level GET to /extensions/github/setup/?installation_id=<attacker> therefore overwrites the victim's in-progress pipeline (SameSite=Lax cookies are sent on that navigation) and then redirects them at GitHub again. The real OAuth callback carries code and state but not installation_id, so GitHubInstallation keeps the poisoned id. A rejected callback has already mutated session state. Bind installation_id only after the OAuth state check succeeds, and do not accept it from an unauthenticated request that is not a completed callback.

true_positives.golden_comment: The AssignmentSource dataclass uses queued: datetime = timezone.now() as a default field value, which evaluates timezone.now() once at class definition time and shares that single datetime instance across all objects.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
queued timestamp is fixed at import, not per assignment

AssignmentSource.queued uses timezone.now() as a dataclass field default. Dataclass defaults are evaluated once when the class is defined, not on each instance, so every AssignmentSource that does not pass queued shares one timestamp: the time this module was imported (the worker/web process start under a preload). The field is then copied into every outbound task payload via to_dict(). Rapid assignee changes, which this PR is meant to disambiguate, all get the same queued time, and any later staleness or ordering check on queued cannot tell them apart. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now). The new tests only assert queued is not None, so they do not catch the shared value.

true_positives.golden_comment: to_dict() returns a datetime for queued; if this dict is passed in task kwargs (e.g., via apply_async), JSON serialization may fail depending on the serializer, which can cause enqueue errors.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Task payload includes a raw datetime and will not round-trip

to_dict() is asdict(self), so assignment_source_dict contains a live datetime under queued. That dict is the Celery kwargs for sync_assignee_outbound (sync.py, the apply_async call). Other arguments on this task are JSON primitives; a JSON Celery serializer raises TypeError when publishing a datetime, so the inbound webhook path (the only caller that sets assignment_source) fails inside GroupAssignee.assign/deassign before any outbound task is queued. Those methods do not catch the error, so the webhook errors and assignee updates are not propagated to other integrations either. from_dict() does cls(**input_dict) and does not parse an ISO string back into a datetime, and nothing calls from_dict(to_dict()) or json-round-trips the payload. Eager task tests bypass the broker serializer, so this stays green. Serialize queued with isoformat() and parse it in from_dict.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The method name has a typo: test_from_dict_inalid_data should be test_from_dict_invalid_data.
Method name says 'empty_array' but tests empty dict - consider renaming to 'test_from_dict_empty_dict' for clarity.

false_positives.candidate:
Cycle guard skips every linked issue on the source integration

should_sync returns False when sync_source.integration_id matches the target installation's integration, and AssignmentSource does not carry the external issue key that triggered the webhook. sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues one task per GroupLink, but each task then drops outbound assignee sync for the whole integration, not just the ticket whose webhook just ran. A Sentry issue linked to two Jira (or other) issues on the same integration will update Sentry and never push the assignee to the other ticket. That echo is not required to stop the loop: an API update on the other ticket webhooks back, assign/deassign sees no assignee change (affected is false / nothing to delete), and outbound stops. The new test only links one external issue, so this regression is untested.

No test that a different integration still syncs outbound

test_assignee_sync_outbound_assign_with_matching_source_integration only asserts that the same integration's sync_assignee_outbound is not called. There is no case with a second linked integration (or a second external issue on another provider) that must still receive the outbound assign, and no matching deassign case. The guard is if sync_source and ids match: return False. A bug that skipped outbound whenever any AssignmentSource was present would still pass this test, which is exactly the non-regression the PR claims (other integrations must keep propagating). Inbound deassign now passes assignment_source too, and nothing asserts that a same-integration unassign does not echo.

true_positives.golden_comment: MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be constructed

MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and only has `pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Instantiating it raises TypeError. It is still wired as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler does `group_type.detector_handler(self)` with no try/except in process_detectors, so any detector whose type resolves to metric_alert_fire crashes the whole batch. The previous handler was a concrete evaluate() that returned no results. Implement the abstract methods (even as explicit stubs) or keep it on DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation exists.

true_positives.golden_comment: Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list

StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], which is the contract change in this PR, but the docstring still says it "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult". Callers and subclass authors will follow the wrong shape.

true_positives.golden_comment: Wrong value `6` passed for `group_2` occurrence — the data packet specifies `"group_2": 10`. Should be `10` to accurately reflect the test scenario, which will ensure the test produces the correct occurrence data.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Expected occurrences are built with the wrong value

Several new assertions build the expected occurrence with a hardcoded value of 6 that is not the value under test: test_state_results_multi_group uses group_2=10 but builds occurrence_2 with 6 (and asserts that payload to Kafka); TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change evaluates 100; TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8. build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores value, so the tests pass without checking that the new hook received the packet value. A later change that includes value in the occurrence will fail for the wrong reason, and a bug that forwards the wrong value will not be caught. Build each expected occurrence with the same group key and value the code evaluates.

true_positives.golden_comment: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Occurrence context ignores rewritten schedule_type

get_monitor_environment_context copies monitor.config and, when schedule_type is present, replaces it with monitor.get_schedule_type_display(). The dict it actually returns uses monitor_environment.monitor.config, not that copy, so the rewrite is discarded. Monitor incident events therefore keep the raw schedule_type (typically an int) instead of the display value the copy was built to provide, and the occurrence payload aliases the monitor's live config dict.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

true_positives.golden_comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Flusher metric shard tags are comma-joined and inconsistent

shard_tag is every shard id for that process joined with commas, and it is sent as a single tag value. The consumer flag defaults to one flusher process, so in production this value is the full assigned-shard list (for example "0,1,2,...,31"). DogStatsD encodes tags as comma-separated key:value pairs, so a comma inside the value splits the metric into garbage tags and drops or mis-attributes spans.buffer.flusher.produce and segment_size_bytes. The tag also changes with every partition assignment, so it cannot be aggregated per shard. wait_produce makes this worse by using the different key "shards" (line 199) while produce uses "shard" (line 185), so the two timers cannot be correlated. Emit one tag value per shard, or omit the tag when a process handles more than one shard, and use the same key on both timers.

true_positives.golden_comment: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Consumer test sleep cannot actually wait for the flusher

test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op at line 15, then calls time.sleep(0.1) specifically to let the flusher thread observe the drift update before join(). That call is the patched no-op, so it does not yield or wait. join() sets stopped immediately; if the flusher has not yet flushed with the new drift, it exits and the assertion that one segment was produced fails intermittently. The production spawn/kill/join path is also untested: produce_to_pipe forces threads, so the SpawnProcess isinstance bug and multi-process flush behavior never run in CI. Wait with a real sleep saved before the patch, and cover at least one multi-shard flush plus process restart.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Hung spawn-context flushers are never killed on Linux

Restart and shutdown treat flusher children as multiprocessing.Process before calling kill() or terminate(). Production processes are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which yields SpawnProcess. On Linux that class is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (the fork context class bound when multiprocessing is imported), so both isinstance checks are false. A hung flusher is therefore left running, and _create_process_for_shards immediately starts another process on the same shards. Both call flush_segments, produce to buffered-segments, and done_flush_segments, so segments are duplicated and Redis flush state races. healthy_since is reset on restart and then updated by the new process, so the hang detector will not notice the leftover process. The same check at join() (line 346) also skips terminate(), so a flusher blocked in Kafka future.result() is not stopped on shutdown. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess, or exclude threading.Thread, instead of multiprocessing.Process.

true_positives.golden_comment: Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.
